Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.label: Acts 26:22
precepts.why:
Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. Don't fall from your own stedfastness: Paul said none other things than Moses and the prophets.

precepts.label: Acts 28:23
precepts.why:
When they appointed Paul a day, many came to his lodging, “to whom he expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” That is the other scriptures. His source material was the Old Testament.

Write this down: Paul's letters predate the gospels, with the exception of Mark. Mark, Luke and Matthew are the synoptic gospels, and it is said Matthew and Luke borrowed from Mark, because Mark was Peter's scribe. That is why Peter has no gospel: Mark is Peter's gospel, and it makes sense that it is the oldest, since Peter's and Paul's ministries were at the same time. Paul's letters range from the forties to the sixties AD. John was written around 90 AD, twenty years after Rome besieged Jerusalem in 70 AD, and Revelation around 95 to 100 AD.

So Paul was not pulling from John 3:16, because when he wrote his letters there was no John 3:16. He was not quoting John, Matthew or Luke; his letters came before them. Luke was travelling with him, and Luke wrote both Luke and Acts: Acts is basically a second Luke, Luke's letter number two.

That is why you cannot understand Paul's letters, the things hard to be understood, without the law and the prophets. Paul persuaded men concerning Jesus out of Moses and the prophets from morning till evening, and the unlearned who don't know those scriptures wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 1:7
precepts.why:
Peter says “our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you”. Peter is giving kudos and respect to Paul for the wisdom that was in him, and that wisdom is Christ, the spirit of Christ. But in Paul's epistles “are some things hard to be understood, which they that are unlearned and unstable wrest”. So first get clear on who Paul was writing to.

“To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.” Called to be saints. Who are the saints? Psalms 148 speaks of “the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him.” The children of Israel are the saints. We are the saints.

Some Christians say Paul was writing to Israelites and other nations at the same time. No. That is not who the letter is addressed to. It is addressed to the saints at Rome. Other nations are never referred to as saints. When you twist that and teach that your oppressor can be granted the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you have been “led away with the error of the wicked” and fallen from your own stedfastness. It is a whole different gospel, and that is how the unlearned wrest Paul unto their own destruction.

precepts.label: Romans 2:17
precepts.why:
Get some clarity on who Paul is writing to: “Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God”. Paul is writing to the Jews. There is obviously northern kingdom in the congregations too, but he is writing to Judah.

Romans 7 says the same: “Know ye not, brethren, (for I speak to them that know the law,)”. Why does he speak to them that know the law? Because he is writing to Jews, “how that the law hath dominion over a man as long as he liveth”.

So Paul is writing to Jews, to those who know the law, to the saints at Rome. Is he addressing both Jews and Gentiles in the church? Yes, but the Gentiles there are the northern kingdom, and they are all saints. He is not writing to other nations at all.

That is why Peter says the unlearned wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”. They stumble because they think Paul was writing things out of thin air to all nations, when he was writing to Israel, men who rested in the law and boasted of God. Know who the letter is addressed to and much of what is hard to be understood in Paul becomes plain.

precepts.label: Romans 15:4
precepts.why:
Christ told the apostles, “behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”, and he is telling us today these things are going to happen to us. How do we know? “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

You read the scripture say we are going to go to jail. You read that we are going to be afflicted, that tribulation is going to hit us. So wherever you find yourself, when these things happen you remember reading it, and you say, I cannot fight it, this is of the Lord. So you humble yourself to see what he is trying to show you.

That is why you cannot be a snake and think you are going to get away with it, selling your soul for nothing, for a little seventy dollars. The day you are sitting in the furnace of the fire, all of it comes back: the evil thoughts toward your brother, smiling in your brother's face while breaking bread, the things you did in secret against the congregation.

You have your own personal demonic sin you are fighting with. Get rid of that first before you think about lining a brother or a sister up for their failure. What was written aforetime was written so that when the trial comes, you have patience and hope, and you stand.

precepts.label: Psalms 140:4
precepts.why:
Christ said “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, and “be thou faithful unto death”. David shows who is working against us: “Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked; preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.”

The purpose of the wicked is to overthrow your goings. You think Satan is sleeping? There is the spiritual Satan and the physical Satan, and every time they are at work, they are working as a team. He will get in your head while you sleep or get in your head while you are awake. At your job, Satan comes jumping into people, and you see people react some type of way.

This is war. That is why you must prepare your soul for the pain that is coming with their children, Esau's children. Whatever state you find yourself in, jail, about to be put to death, afflicted, tortured, losing an eye or an arm, be faithful, because pain is part of the walk. The body is not you; your soul is you.

Mark 9 shows how that spirit works in us: “ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. That is us destroying ourselves in the club, the partying and religion, because Satan is in us and we thought it was the way. So pray to be kept from the hands of the wicked, and ask the Lord to strengthen your faith, because when your faith is weak, Satan keeps attacking you.

classes.title: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:5
precepts.why:
“And when he had opened the fourth seal”: this is the time we are living in right now. The fifth seal is the saints being killed; we haven't met that time yet, but it is approaching. Then “behold a pale horse: and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him.” This is talking about America. “And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth”: the Americas are called the fourth part of the world. That is the Monroe Doctrine, revised as the Donroe Doctrine, and the Bible talks about it.

Habakkuk explains the hell and death: “Behold, his soul which is lifted up is not upright in him”. This is America. “Yea also, because he transgresseth by wine”, and wine is falsehood and lies, “he is a proud man, neither keepeth at home”: he is in every country. He is one “who enlargeth his desire as hell”: he wants the oil, the minerals, the rare earths, the resources. He “is as death”, because when he comes through he brings death. He “cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations”: all nations are living here in America.

So Death and Hell riding over the fourth part of the earth is America, never satisfied, killing “with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.” War, famine, death, and the beasts of the earth, which is zoonosis: gain-of-function research taking diseases from monkeys, bats and animals and making viruses that kill us. America is returning to its old colonizing, oppressive nature, keeping dominance over this side of the world, where our people are.

precepts.label: Matthew 24:6
precepts.why:
What does it mean that the pale horse was given power “to kill with sword”? Christ said: “And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars”, and a lot of those wars and rumours of wars are going to be started by America. Then, “see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet.”

“For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom”. Kingdoms are superpowers: Russia, Europe, America. They will fight each other; Russia and NATO will fight. Then, “there shall be famines, and pestilences”: famine and diseases, the same thing we read in Revelation 6, the hunger and the beasts of the earth. “All these are the beginning of sorrows.”

Everything we read in Revelation 6 is here in Matthew 24, and the next part says they will deliver us up to be killed, which goes into the fifth seal. The wars, rumours of wars and famines take place because of that pale horse, America. We are living in the beginning of sorrows during the fourth seal, and it is going to get worse and worse, beyond the worst things you can think of. Don't sit back comfortable because nothing has happened to you yet. You thought World War II was bad; wait until you see what is about to happen on this earth.

thread.label: Revelation 7:1-8
thread.text: And after these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor on any tree.

classes.title: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 13:5
precepts.why:
Four angels hold the four winds of the earth, and another angel cries to them, “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.” The four winds are held back for a reason, and Ezra shows what gathers from those four winds.

“And after this I beheld, and, lo, there was gathered together a multitude of men, out of number, from the four winds of the heaven, to subdue the man that came out of the sea.” That multitude out of number is their military, gathered from the four winds to fight against Christ, the man that came out of the sea.

So the holding of the winds is this: do not let war pop off to the max until the servants of God are sealed. The armies of the nations are held back until the leaders of Israel, the hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes, are sealed with the law of God in Christ.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:16
precepts.why:
The angel ascending from the east has “the seal of the living God”, and the servants of our God are sealed in their foreheads. What is that seal? Isaiah says it: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” That is the seal of the living God: the law, sealed among his disciples, in Christ.

And the ones sealed are “an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel”, twelve thousand of every tribe, from Juda to Benjamin. These are the leaders; the 144,000 is just the leading men. In order for them to be sealed, they have to know who they are, at least to some extent.

So how are you going to read that and be confused about the twelve tribes? You just read all of the tribes right there. You can't make this stuff up.

precepts.label: Obadiah 1:15-17
precepts.why:
“And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus”. The woman is Babylon the Great, America, and the martyrs of Jesus are the Israelites: those who stand up for this truth all the way up to the threat of death and beyond it. Many of us are going to get killed. They drank our blood by putting us in captivity and dealing evil with us.

Obadiah explains that drinking: “For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.” The reward of what the nations did to us is coming back on them. “For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain”: what did they drink upon us? Captivity, slavery, rape, robbery, murder, lies, rigged juries, castrations, lynchings, railroading; the Rasheem Carters, the Kendrick Johnsons.

“So shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down”. All the nations that did this to God’s people will drink the captivity, the slavery, the whipped backs, the lynchings, and digest it. “And they shall be as though they had not been.” They dehumanized us until we do not even recognize we were once a great people, reduced us to nothing, when we are the jewels of God. So they will be reduced to nothing, as Isaiah 14:21 cuts off their name.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.” Deliverance is for the ones of us that repent and stop BSing. The ones who do not repent and keep up the BS, the Most High is going to wipe out along with our enemies.

precepts.label: Isaiah 13:5
precepts.why:
“The beast that thou sawest was, and is not; and shall ascend out of the bottomless pit, and go into perdition”. It was in John’s vision but not in his time. When it came, it came out of Europe, Great Britain to be exact. And it shall go into perdition, destruction. That is where we are now; that is what this war is signifying.

The weapons to do it are already here. You don’t have to wonder where the fire is going to come from. The Lord will come with fire because he is coming with those weapons; he is going to be literally riding on the weapons being fired, and coming with something like two hundred million angels. That is what Isaiah 13:5 says: the Lord and the weapons of his indignation come from a far country, “to destroy the whole land”, the whole land, singular.

That fire is the perdition of Babylon the Great; that is what the beast is going to get. And “they that dwell on the earth shall wonder, whose names were not written in the book of life”. They have no clue that this is Babylon the Great, and they are not getting the kingdom, no matter how many churches they set up.

Every time you pray the Lord’s prayer, thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth, you are advocating for the destruction of this kingdom. Christ is not setting his kingdom beside this one. The King of kings is coming to topple it with the weapons of his indignation.

precepts.label: Hebrews 12:1
precepts.why:
The Lord says to them who keep his commandments and precepts, “let not your sins weigh you down.” Sin feels good. The pleasure comes, and once the pleasure is gone the guilt rolls in, and you feel like crap. After a while it becomes a burden, and it shows on you. Many of us came into the school guilty of things too shameful to confess, and some are still doing them. When you come forward and confess, you feel that weight lifted off: thank God.

Paul uses the same picture: “Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us.” Lay aside every weight. Your sins of character are weights.

If you run a race carrying weights, can you run fast? No. You can still be in the race, but you either keep adding weight until you come in last and never cross the finish line, or you take the weights off. One weight off and you feel lighter; another off and you are faster. You were in third, now second, now first.

Some of y’all say, I’m good back here, I’ll just walk. Meanwhile you are on a timer, and time at the end is running out. A race is won by the time you run. If you are walking in a race, you are not winning at all, by no account.

That is why we lay aside every weight: the sins that so easily beset us are what hold us back. It is what 2 Esdras means: do not let your sins weigh you down.

precepts.why:
Why is it that when our iniquity had an end, Esau refused to let us go and kept shedding our blood? Solomon speaks of the ancient Egyptians, and this is modern Egypt today: “not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.” Their malice is bred in them: God made them that way. They will never change as a race of people. That's why it has been a perpetual hatred from Cain to Abel, Jacob to Esau, blacks and whites, playing itself out over and over, while Christianity blinds us from accepting what God is telling us.

Name a century that black people have had pure peace around this white man. Not we-got-the-vote peace: you still get jailed, racially profiled, shot down, and you can't do what white people do when they get pulled over. The record lists it: the transatlantic slave trade and child slavery from 1619 to 1865, racial terror after emancipation, massacres in Memphis, Colfax, Wilmington, Atlanta, East St. Louis, the Red Summer, Arkansas, Tulsa, Rosewood. And that is only what was reported; imagine what was not documented.

As a result of all this enslavement and all these massacres, Esau is thinking a certain way now. He thinks he's getting away with it: “These things hast thou done, and I kept silence.” Oh, wait a minute, we just enslaved the Lord's people and he didn't do anything.

“thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself.” That is what Esau is thinking to this day. That's why they don't hold themselves accountable for anything. They hold themselves not guilty when they slay us, when they kill us, when they put us into slavery, when they don't give us reparations. Esau thinks he is God.

“but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” There will be a judgment for these things. So don't think that smiling white man in your face means to do you good.

precepts.label: Sirach 19:20
precepts.why:
Sirach 15:15 says, “If thou wilt, to keep the commandments, and to perform acceptable faithfulness.” Keeping God's commandments is performing acceptable faithfulness: those are your actions, and that is where your faith lies. Your works prove your faith and your faith proves your works; they go hand in hand. God “hath set fire and water before thee: stretch forth thy hand unto whether thou wilt.”

For anyone still confused, Sirach 19:20 says it again: “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.” The performance of the law is the acceptable faithfulness of Sirach 15. Wisdom is not only knowing the law; it is performing it.

The words “the knowledge of his omnipotency” mean knowing that God is all around us, and we acknowledge it by keeping his laws.

This is what Habakkuk and Paul mean by the just living by faith. Paul says “the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The just are those who keep God's laws and commandments, and they live by faith in Christ. Fearing God, keeping his law and living by faith are one walk.

precepts.label: Genesis 26:5
precepts.why:
God told Isaac why the promise stood: “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” Abraham obeyed, and he kept the charge, the commandments, the statutes and the laws. That is past tense. It tells you what Abraham was doing from the beginning that proved his faith. His obedience was his acceptable faithfulness, the performance of Sirach 15:15.

Paul writes, “And the law is not of faith: but, The man that doeth them shall live in them.” The law meant there is the law of sacrifice, which came later. Abraham's faith came first, and his faith and the promise to him go hand in hand; the promise predates the law of sacrifice.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us”. The curse of the law is condemnation, not being able to atone for every sin. Caiaphas pointed it out without knowing it: “it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” Both the northern and southern kingdoms were under the old covenant they agreed to in Deuteronomy 27 and kept breaking, so both were condemned and destroyed by the nations. But the Lord loved them, sent his son to die for them, and took them out of that contract into a new one, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ”, meaning the northern kingdom.

Paul says “before faith came, we were kept under the law”, and “the law was our schoolmaster to bring us unto Christ, that we might be justified by faith.” The schoolmaster is the law of sacrifice, and the “we” is Israel. After faith came, “we are no longer under a schoolmaster.” Jews, Greeks, bond, free, male and female were all the same people of God in Christ.

“And if ye be Christ’s, then are ye Abraham’s seed, and heirs according to the promise.” Abraham is the father of faith, so his children should be children of faith like him: keeping the commandments the way he did, with faith in Christ instead of the animal sacrifice the Galatians were bewitched back into. The promise pertains to the Israelites, not to all nations.

precepts.label: Romans 7:12
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Thou therefore, O Lord, that art the God of the just, hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Obviously: if you are just, you have nothing to repent from. But what makes you just?

Paul answers it: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” The law is holy, and the commandment is holy, just and good. When you are applying it, that is what makes you just. That is what makes you good: the law and the commandment.

So the God of the just is the God of those who keep the commandments, “as to Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, which have not sinned against thee.” They kept God’s laws. Repentance was not appointed for them.

“But thou hast appointed repentance unto me that am a sinner.” Manasseh knew he was not just. He had broken the holy, just and good commandment on every count, and his only hope was the repentance the Lord appoints unto sinners.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 1:9-11
precepts.why:
Manasseh says the God of the just “hast not appointed repentance to the just.” Paul says the same exact thing: “Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient.” The law is not made for a righteous man, just as repentance is not appointed for the just.

It is made “for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind”, that is homosexuality, “for menstealers”, child traffickers, “for liars, for perjured persons”, liars under oath before the judge, “and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine”, anything not listed.

“According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.” The law is in accordance with the gospel. You cannot have one without the other.

That list is Manasseh. Under the law of Moses he was condemned on all accounts: he killed babies, he was an idolater and a murderer, he shed the blood of children from one end of Jerusalem to the other, and he was steeped in every evil. He was America, but a king; Epstein, but a king; King Diddy Manasseh. There was no animal he could sacrifice. He was a king worthy of death, and his mindset was, I’m the king, I do what I want. The Lord said, you’re the king? Cool, and threw him in prison.

Yet the Lord appointed repentance unto him, and let him live as an example to us in this time. Most kings and celebrities with that status will not repent. When you are rich you become your own god; they literally call them idols. Oprah said on air she does not respect a jealous God. But Manasseh humbled himself, and that is the lesson.

precepts.label: Luke 18:9-14
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “I am not worthy to behold and see the height of heaven for the multitude of mine iniquities.” Many of us think this. Christ gives a parable about that very man, spoken “unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others.” Those who were righteous in their own eyes and despised everybody else were the Pharisees: I'm more righteous than you, you're wicked.

“Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.” The publican was a tax collector, and they were praying in the same place. The Pharisee thanked God he was “not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican”, not like this dude next to him, and bragged, “I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.”

“And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven.” Why? Because he felt unworthy, the same as Manasseh, who could not behold the height of heaven. He “smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner”: the same thing Manasseh said in his prayer, my sins are a multitude.

Christ's judgment: “this man went down to his house justified rather than the other.” The sinner who asked for mercy went home justified; the one who called himself righteous did not. “for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased”: that is what Manasseh did in the beginning, exalting himself, and he was brought down to a low condition, locked up and imprisoned. “and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted”: that is Manasseh later on, after he humbled himself.

So humble yourself and you will be exalted. Exalt yourself and you will be humbled, and you are not going to like that humbling either.

precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Manasseh confesses, “I did not thy will, neither kept I thy commandments.” Those two go together, because the Lord's will is his commandments. David shows it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

To do God's will is to have his law in your heart. The laws of God are the will of God; God's will is his laws. So when Manasseh says he did not God's will, he is saying the same thing twice: he did not keep the commandments. Not doing the will of God is not some mystery feeling; it is breaking his law.

That is why Manasseh goes straight on to say, “I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.” He had provoked the Lord's wrath and done evil before him, and he was bowed down with iron bands, locked up with no release. A man who delights to do God's will keeps the law within his heart; Manasseh had to come to that by being humbled, bowing the knee of his heart and acknowledging his iniquity.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 2:4-17
precepts.why:
Manasseh begs, “forgive me, O Lord, forgive me, and destroy me not with mine iniquites. Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me.” What does he mean by reserving evil for you? There is evil reserved for you while you keep playing around. Peter shows it.

“For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.” These are the angels that fell in Adam’s time, cast down to destruction. Remember David said, take not thy holy spirit from me. If the Lord removes his Holy Spirit from you, you are now in chains of darkness, reserved unto judgment.

“The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished.” Manasseh said, don’t reserve evil for me, because the Lord reserves punishment for the unjust. “But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.” Chiefly means primarily. Despising government is despising leadership. When leadership is trying to help you and you say, nah, I know what I’m doing, you are not humble. Your heart is arrogant.

They follow “the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness”: money. “These are wells without water, clouds that are carried with a tempest”, carried about by different doctrines, all over the place, “to whom the mist of darkness is reserved for ever.” The mist of darkness is the reprobate mind; the Holy Spirit is not in them. That is evil reserved for them.

So Manasseh, a king worthy of that very judgment, humbled himself and asked the Lord not to reserve that evil for him. We must do the same while repentance is open.

precepts.label: 2 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “Be not angry with me for ever, by reserving evil for me; neither condemn me to the lower parts of the earth.” Peter shows the great evil reserved at the end: “But the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men.”

The heavens and the earth are reserved unto fire: nuclear fire, and the hellfire that follows after it. That is what the ungodly are reserved for, and that is what Manasseh was asking not to be reserved for him. The lower parts of the earth he speaks of go into the hellfire again.

Then he says, “For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent.” He is the God of them that repent. Unto them that repent he grants return. So humble yourself before you are sick, examine yourself before judgment, and in the time of sins show repentance, because the fire is already reserved for the ungodly.

precepts.label: Sirach 17:24
precepts.why:
Manasseh prays, “For thou art the God, even the God of them that repent; and in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.” He is the God of them that repent.

Sirach shows what he does for them: “But unto them that repent, he granted them return, and comforted those that failed in patience.” Unto them that repent he grants return, return to the land. And he comforts those who failed in patience.

That is the goodness Manasseh expected God to show in him. He was unworthy, a king condemned on every count, but he repented, and the Lord brought him back again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. So it is for Israel as a nation: Manasseh is the living embodiment of the nation, and if we repent, he grants us return.

precepts.label: Sirach 18:20-21
precepts.why:
Manasseh humbled himself in his affliction, and the Lord saved him, unworthy as he was, “according to thy great mercy.” Sirach tells us to do it before the day comes: “Before judgment examine thyself, and in the day of visitation thou shalt find mercy.”

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the day of visitation you will find grace and mercy. “Humble thyself before thou be sick, and in the time of sins shew repentance.”

Manasseh waited until he was bound in fetters in Babylon before he humbled himself. Don’t wait until you are sick, locked up, or exposed. In the time of wrong, show repentance, and the same mercy Manasseh found will be there for you.

precepts.label: Matthew 3:2-8
precepts.why:
The Lord is “the God of them that repent”, and repentance is the first thing preached when the kingdom draws near: “Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.” It was the first thing Christ said in his preaching, and it goes for all of us.

John the Baptist cried it: “For this is he that was spoken of by the prophet Esaias, saying, The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” He wore “raiment of camel’s hair, and a leathern girdle about his loins; and his meat was locusts and wild honey.” And “Jerusalem, and all Judea, and all the region round about Jordan” came out and were baptized of him in Jordan, “confessing their sins.”

“But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath to come?” What are you doing here? “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”: fruits suitable for repentance.

That is the fig tree in Luke 13, dunged and dug about so that it may bring forth fruit. That was John’s ministry, paving the way for Christ. Manasseh did not only say sorry; he confessed his sins and his life changed. That is repentance with fruit.

precepts.label: Matthew 9:11-13
precepts.why:
Manasseh says, “thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.” Christ came for exactly such as him. “And when the Pharisees saw it, they said unto his disciples, Why eateth your Master with publicans and sinners?” It is the same spirit as the Pharisee in Luke 18: I’m more righteous than this publican over here.

“But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.” That is exactly what Manasseh said: the just need no repentance. The sick are the ones the law is made for, the lawless and the whoremongers.

“But go ye and learn what that meaneth”: go learn what that means, you guys are stupid. “I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” He is quoting Hosea. God cares about mercy more than sacrifice. “For I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”

God is the God of those that repent. Manasseh had no sacrifice that could cover him under the law, but he found mercy, because Christ came to call sinners like him to repentance.

precepts.label: Hosea 6:6
precepts.why:
When the Pharisees asked why Christ ate with publicans and sinners, he told them, “But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.” He was quoting Hosea: “For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.”

God doesn’t care about sacrifice the way the Pharisees did. He cares about mercy. He desires mercy, and the knowledge of God, more than burnt offerings.

That is why Manasseh could be saved. Under the law there was no animal he could sacrifice to cover what he had done; he was finished. But the Lord desired mercy and not sacrifice, and so Manasseh could pray, “in me thou wilt shew all thy goodness: for thou wilt save me, that am unworthy, according to thy great mercy.”

precepts.label: Matthew 4:15
precepts.why:
“The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles”. Zebulun and Naphtali are tribes of Israel, part of the northern kingdom, and yet their land is called Galilee of the Gentiles. So the southern kingdom was calling the northern kingdom Gentiles and uncircumcised. Very simple.

How did Israelites come to be called Gentiles? In the days of the Maccabees, “according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised. And they hanged the infants about their necks”. They were enforcing it: you could not be circumcised; you had to be like the Gentiles. They were hanging babies. So what is the next generation going to be? Uncircumcised. And the next one, uncircumcised, not keeping the laws, profaning the Sabbath, calling themselves and being called Gentiles.

Zondervan's compact Bible dictionary says Gentiles usually means a non-Israelite people. Usually: meaning there are certain contexts, like this one, where it is not talking about the other nations at all, but about Israelites who were made to live like the heathen. That is how Ephesians 2 has to be understood.
